page.layout: One printed page, running text in the centre with no margin notes. Top: running head and page number. Then a title and a Latin poem, followed by its signature. Below a rule: a second poem with a title, a drop-capped text and its signature.

main_text.l: EPITAPHIVM DVORVM
FRATRVM GEMELLORVM,
qui eadem hora mortui sunt &
eodem sepulchro conditi.
Uno cur tumulo fratrum composita duorum
Funera funt, quaeris? Carmina nostra lege.
Vera loquor: fratres eadem parit hora gemellos,
Ambo pares studiis, moribus ambo pares,
Vox eadem, gestus, vultus, facies, color idem,

l.i: Alter & alterius par in amore fuit:

main_text.l: Et (magè quod mirere) malis vexatus eisdem,
Et morbis paribus semper uterque fuit.
Et tandem fratres eadem abstulit hora gemellos:
Sic vita similis mors quoque facta fuit.
Ne fierent igitur post mortem conditione
Dissimiles, eadem nunc capit urna duos.
I. I. B.
Comitis cuiusdam Scoti Epitaphium.
NOxne an clara dies habet hic sua limina? non
nox: Clarus enim nostræ nobilitatis honos.
Vitam alto repetere labor non magnus Olympo,
Invenies gelido condita membra solo.
L. j.

page.notes: The first poem's title is set in capitals and the second's in a smaller title; both were treated as poem titles, the first at level 1 and the second at level 2. The scan is faint in places: "quaeris" and "facta" in the first poem, and "non" at the end of the second poem's first line, are read with some doubt. No margin notes, no catchword and no signature mark are visible. Long s was normalised to s and u/v to the vowel/consonant forms. The æ ligature in "nostræ" is kept as printed.
